If KMT2A and KMT2F localize to rDNA and interact with the RNA polymerase I machinery through their methyltransferase activity, then their depletion or catalytic inactivation will reduce RNA Pol I occupancy, histone H3K4 methylation, and rRNA synthesis because they directly recruit and/or stabilize RNA Pol I at ribosomal DNA.

If KMT2A and KMT2F are recruited to rDNA through direct interaction with the RNA polymerase I transcription machinery, then depletion or catalytic inactivation of these methyltransferases will reduce rRNA transcription and RNA Pol I/UBF occupancy at rDNA because their H3K4 methyltransferase activity is required to establish active chromatin at the rDNA locus.

If KMT2A and KMT2F associate with RNA polymerase I machinery at rDNA promoter-proximal regions and methylate H3K4, then loss of their catalytic activity or rDNA binding will reduce RNA Pol I occupancy, H3K4me2/3 enrichment, and pre-rRNA synthesis at nucleolar rDNA loci.
